drivingQuestion: Why does R' Elazar accept the first tanna when the husband's agent changes place but dissent when the wife's agent does?
outcomeNote: the distinction rests on the husband's volition versus the wife's

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר – מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא דְּלָא פְּלִיג, וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא דִּפְלִיג?
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara asks: «And» according to «Rabbi Elazar, what is different» in «the first clause,» where the agent deviated from the husband’s instructions and delivered the bill of divorce in a different place, «where he does not disagree» with the unattributed opinion of the first tanna that the divorce is invalid, «and what is different» in «the latter clause,» where the agent deviated from the wife’s instructions and received the bill of divorce in a different place, «where he disagrees» with the unattributed opinion of the first tanna and deems the divorce valid?

segments.he: אִיהוּ, דְּמִדַּעְתֵּיהּ מְגָרֵשׁ – קָפֵיד, אִיהִי, דִּבְעַל כֻּרְחַהּ מִתְגָּרֶשֶׁת – מַרְאָה מָקוֹם הִיא לוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «He,» the husband, «who divorces» his wife «of his own volition, insists» that the divorce be effected in a certain place. However, «she,» the wife, «who is divorced» even «against her will,» is in no position to insist with regard to the manner in which the divorce will be effected, and «is» merely «indicating a place for him» to give her the bill of divorce.
